title: The Grave of Scenarios
html:
White Pure energy pounded against my heart, and blood surged through my body like a flagship fitted with a new engine.

[The exclusive skill, ‘Electrification (電人化) Lv.11(+1)’, has been activated.]

Perhaps because my Status had risen, Electrification’s skill level had reached 11.

Normally, all skills capped at level 10. Beyond that, your only options were to learn a better skill or use ‘transcendence’ like the returnees. But level 11?

My [Electrification] had now surpassed the system’s limits.

Ruuuumble.

On top of that, using Electrification wasn’t as difficult as it used to be.

The returnee Kyrgios possessed power comparable to that of powerful Narrative-grade constellations. Before, he had been so formidable that I couldn’t even fathom the depths of his strength. Now, though, I felt I could understand a little of how powerful he was.

If Kyrgios had once stood on a summit I could never reach, perhaps now I could vaguely guess where he stood up there.

Tentacio had gone beyond shock. Now he was terrified.

“A constellation’s Status and a returnee’s martial arts? What the hell are you!”

I was about to tell him my name, but on a petty impulse, I tried saying this instead.

“······What else would I be? You said I was Yoo Joonghyuk.”

Bzzzzzt!

With Electrification’s explosive power added to it, the Blade of Faith tore Tentacio’s body in two. Electricity scattered by the next strike blew his arms and legs apart, and the third strike sent his head flying before it rolled across the ground. A sequence of blows that hadn’t even given him time to scream. My level 90 Magic Power drained away all at once, leaving me faintly tired. But now I knew exactly where I stood.

“Kgh······ Yoo Joonghyuk······.”

Fuck, that startled me.

The severed head was talking.

“Do you know······ what it means······ for an incarnation to become a constellation?”

What was this bullshit all of a sudden?

“You will regret······ telling me your name······.”

“What?”

[Demon Count ‘Tentacio’ has used ‘Death Scream’.]

[Demon Count ‘Tentacio’ has spread the name ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’ throughout the Dark Castle.]

[The Dark Castle’s rankers have remembered the name ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’.]

······I hadn’t expected this.

[The Dark Castle’s rankers bare their teeth at Incarnation ‘Yoo Joonghyuk’.]

Well, now I felt a little bad.

I really hadn’t meant for this to happen.

But Yoo Joonghyuk ought to suffer a little, too.

[You have hunted ‘Demon Count Tentacio’!]

[You have earned 30000 coins for being the fifth to defeat a grade-3 demon.]

When Tentacio died, transparent strings of text began rising from his corpse.

Starting with the [Dark Castle] scenario, you could kill beings who possessed Stories and take those Stories from them.

I reached out and snatched the text.

[You have acquired the Historical-grade Story ‘Bug Slaughter’.]

[Bug Slaughter].

This should be a good enough Story to give the forty-first-round Shin Yoosung, who was still incubating.

······But was it all right to feed her a Story that had belonged to a demon? What if feeding her the wrong thing made her turn bad?

[You have completed the bounty scenario!]

[The constellation ‘Supreme Maegum’ is deeply grateful to you.]

[You can now receive the protection of ‘constellations from Silla’.]

Protection from the constellations of Silla.

They might seem insignificant, but they were still ‘constellations’. If I built ties with them, a day would surely come when they could help me, as they had with the [Absolute Throne].

[You have received the Historical-grade Story, ‘Silla-Tang Allied Army’.]

······Silla-Tang Allied Army?

[The constellation, ‘Supreme Maegum’, smiles contentedly.]

Well, they’d said they would give me a Historical-grade Story. They hadn’t said it would be a good one.

If necessary, I could feed this to Shin Yoosung, too.

Having recovered their senses, my companions approached from behind, one by one.

“Fuck, that was insane, Kim Dokja······.”

“Dokja-ssi, just how strong have you become······?”

I smiled awkwardly.

Lee Hyunsung looked down at the shoulder Tentacio had injured and asked,

“······Are there many beings like this on the second floor?”

“There’ll be some, but they won’t be common. This one’s ranking was probably······.”

Just then, a message sounded from the air.

[You have earned 50000 coins as a main scenario reward!]

[The main scenario’s contents are being updated!]

[You have won the Dark Castle placement match.]

[The demon you hunted was ‘Tentacio’, ranked 10th in the Dark Castle.]

[Rankings are being assigned in proportion to your contributions to the hunt.]

“······He was 10th. That would mean there are at least nine others stronger than him. There’ll be even more at about his level, though.”

“Ah······.”

Lee Hyunsung’s expression was complicated. He seemed both relieved and disheartened that the demon count had been ranked 10th.

“You’ve become strong enough to fight beings like that, Dokja-ssi··.”

“Once you finish inheriting your Story, Hyunsung-ssi, you’ll be able to do it, too. And even I can’t guarantee a win against demons stronger than this one.”

In my current state, ‘count-class’ was the limit of what I could fight without releasing my Stories.

Even then, it wouldn’t have been this easy if his Story hadn’t been [Bug Slaughter].

Han Sooyoung furrowed her brow, as though her pride had been hurt.

“Tch, pretending to be humble······ Are you trying to make fools of us?”

“You would’ve had a decent shot if you’d fought at full strength, too. Aren’t you inheriting the Black Flame Dragon’s Story?”

“The Story is so cringeworthy that I haven’t been able to inherit it yet. You deliberately didn’t stop me when I said I was choosing this one, didn’t you? Just to screw me over?”

What was the Story of the ‘Abyssal Black Flame Dragon’ again······?

I couldn’t quite remember, but considering that its original contractor had been ‘Delusion Demon Kim Namwoon’, Han Sooyoung’s reaction wasn’t incomprehensible.

It was surely a Story that made you feel so ashamed merely by inheriting it that your soul seemed to vanish.

[The Dark Castle rankings will now be announced in proportion to your contributions to the hunt!]

At last, the rankings had been calculated.

The results were sent to the windows that appeared before each of us.

[Incarnation Kim Dokja’s Dark Castle ranking is ‘11th’.]

11th.

Not a bad result for a placement match.

The rest of my companions looked devastated, as though they’d just received their college entrance exam results.

Han Sooyoung hurried over and peeked at my ranking window.

“Hey, what rank did you······.”

Han Sooyoung froze when she saw the number ‘11’.

The difference in our contributions had been enormous, so Han Sooyoung and I were probably at least several hundred places apart now.

“······If I kill you now, do I become 11th?”

“What rank are you?”

“Not telling. Anyway, I’m higher than that guy.”

Han Sooyoung pointed at the unconscious Kim Yongpal.

[Incarnation Kim Yongpal’s Dark Castle ranking is ‘101123rd’.]

Kim Yongpal, who had placed 101123rd, was sleeping without a care in the world.

Lee Jihye and Lee Gilyoung, who had been unconscious from the start, had placed 98761st and 87541st respectively. Looking at it this way, that was strange. Why was that guy ranked lower than people who’d been unconscious the whole time?

“What rank are you, Lee Hyunsung-ssi?”

“636th.”

Lee Hyunsung sounded gloomy. I briefly hesitated, wondering whether I should offer some consolation, but he spoke first.

“······I received plenty of report cards like this at school, so I’m fine. Somehow, I feel even more motivated.”

It seemed there was no particular need to worry.

Right, Lee Hyunsung was the type to work even harder once he had a concrete goal.

Shin Yoosung, who was standing nearby, recoiled in surprise when our eyes met.

“D-don’t look!”

The way she hastily hid her window was exactly like an elementary school student hiding a report card from her parents. I gave some thought to how I could avoid hurting her feelings.

“Your rank right now isn’t what matters. There’ll be plenty of chances to rise once we reach the second floor. It all depends on how hard you work, Yoosung.”

······Damn it. Now that I’d said it, I couldn’t have sounded more like a preachy old fart.

Everything would work out if you tried hard enough? Of course it wouldn’t.

But the kindhearted Shin Yoosung seemed to take my advice to heart.

“······If I work hard, can I become as strong as you, ajusshi?”

“Of course. You can become even stronger than me.”

I meant what I said.

In fact, Shin Yoosung was an incarnation with more potential than anyone else here.

[Your stigma is about to bloom.]

[A Story is being selected to become your stigma.]

If I could just pass on a stigma, Shin Yoosung’s growth would be explosive.

No, even without a stigma, Shin Yoosung was essential on the Dark Castle’s second floor. There was a stage there where the children could shine.

“But I don’t understand why we’ve suddenly been given these rankings. Is it simply to encourage competition······ or do they give us medals if we reach the higher ranks?”

It was Lee Hyunsung who said that.

He wasn’t wrong. That was surely part of the purpose.

But there was a much more fundamental reason for the Dark Castle’s rankings.

At the very moment I was about to speak.

[The Demon King, ‘Asmodeus’, finds your existence intriguing.]

[The Demon King, ‘Astaroth’, has his eye on you all.]

[The Demon King, ‘Orobas’, smacks his lips at your Stories.]

It seemed my companions had received messages, too.

Messages steeped in a far stickier, more sinister feeling than those we received from constellations.

My companions were trembling, having sensed their Status from the messages alone.

Han Sooyoung in particular, who had once received a ‘Demon King’s Curse’, looked utterly terrified.

Demon Kings.

Among living beings, the exceedingly few demons whose ‘Status’ could rival that of constellations.

At the end of this scenario, we would fight a Demon King.

●

“Gaaaaagh!”

The blade that had severed the demon’s head traced a beautiful arc back into Yoo Joonghyuk’s hand.

‘······This one had no Story.’

Having already reached the second floor, Yoo Joonghyuk had begun working on his ranking in earnest.

As always, his plans for the future were densely laid out in his mind like a daily training schedule.

‘To reach the third floor, I must first recruit the Four Heavenly Kings.’

‘I need to bring the highest-ranking individuals over to my side.’

‘One of the 10 Evils is on the second floor. I’d be better off avoiding a clash with him.’

‘If I keep collecting Stories at this pace, probably within four days······.’

That was when a message sounded from the air.

[Someone has spread your name using ‘Death Scream’.]

[The Dark Castle’s rankers have remembered your name.]

[The Dark Castle’s rankers are wary of you.]

[The Dark Castle’s rankers will target your Stories.]

Yoo Joonghyuk frowned at the unexpected messages.

‘My name has suddenly become known?’

It was strange.

‘[Death Scream] is a demon’s curse. I haven’t killed any demons with that ability yet.’

Beside him, Yoo Mia puffed out her cheeks and asked,

“What’s wrong, oppa?”

“Nothing.”

After a moment’s hesitation, Yoo Joonghyuk added,

“······It seems that guy is going around causing trouble again.”

“That guy?”

“Someone I know.”

Yoo Mia quietly watched her brother cut the conversation short in a cold voice.

There was clearly something different in the tone of his grumbling. The change was as small as the germ of a grain of rice, but Yoo Mia could detect it.

Because Yoo Joonghyuk was her one and only brother.

“You mean that ugly ajusshi, right?”

“······.”

“You look happy when you talk about him, oppa.”

Flustered by his little sister’s broad grin, Yoo Joonghyuk snapped,

“You’re mistaken.”

“Am I?”

Yoo Mia simply watched him with a quiet smile.

Frowning, Yoo Joonghyuk started to say something, then closed his mouth.

The next moment, a murderous aura flowed from his entire body. Just as Yoo Mia was about to speak, wondering if he was angry, Yoo Joonghyuk spoke first.

“Stop eavesdropping and come out. Before I kill you.”

At his words, part of the space seemed to stiffen. Then, with a cracking sound, a slender human figure appeared through the split in space. It was a woman wearing a cape.

“I’m sorry. I didn’t mean to.”

“Who are you?”

“It’s me, Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi.”

When she removed the cape, an unexpected person was revealed.

It was a face Yoo Joonghyuk knew, too.

Because she was someone he had saved not long ago.

“······Yoo Sangah?”

Yoo Sangah, an incarnation sponsored by the <nebula> Olympus, stood there.

Seeing her for the first time in a week, Yoo Joonghyuk thought she looked even more haggard than before.

But the intelligence shining in her eyes was more brilliant than ever.

“It seems you’ve inherited some rather good Stories.”

Yoo Joonghyuk slowly drew the [Splitting the Sky Sword].

The Dark Castle’s second floor was a suitable stage for stealing other people’s Stories.

And Yoo Sangah’s Stories were well worth taking.

‘This woman wasn’t in the previous round, either.’

He’d had his reasons last time, but he couldn’t leave such uncertainties alone forever. Kim Dokja alone was already more than enough to deal with. Yoo Sangah raised both hands slightly and stepped back.

“I haven’t come to fight.”

“Then why are you here?”

“I need help.”

“I told you not to involve yourself with me again. Saving you then was merely repayment of my debt to Kim Dokja.”

“This concerns that very Kim Dokja-ssi.”

For a moment, Yoo Joonghyuk’s murderous intent eased.

“······What do you mean?”

As the oppressive aura around them vanished, Yoo Sangah took a short breath and spoke.

“In this scenario, Dokja-ssi will die.”

Kim Dokja would die?

Yoo Joonghyuk gave a little scoff.

“Kim Dokja can resurrect. I believe I told you before. Apparently, you weren’t listening.”

By now, Yoo Joonghyuk had some idea of Kim Dokja’s abilities. Of course, he probably couldn’t resurrect indefinitely, but he would be able to come back at least a few more times. That meant Kim Dokja’s life would not be in danger for a while.

“He should have revived by now······ It seems you haven’t met him yet?”

This time, Yoo Sangah’s gaze wavered.

But she persisted and spoke again.

“That isn’t what I mean. If we leave things as they are, Dokja-ssi will ‘really’ die.”

“······How do you know that?”

“Because I saw it.”

“You saw it?”

The next moment, a massive skein of thread appeared behind Yoo Sangah.

It was not [Ariadne]’s skein.

On closer inspection, the threads of the skein were not made of fibers. Tiny strings of text. Cords woven from countless stories. Yoo Joonghyuk knew that shape, embroidering the air like an enormous fabric of fate.

And because he knew it, he couldn’t help being shocked.

Because it was the symbol of the three goddesses of fate, the Moerae.

Yoo Joonghyuk spoke through gritted teeth.

“Don’t tell me you stole a look at the constellations’ prophecy?”

Yoo Sangah nodded cautiously.

Enraged, Yoo Joonghyuk said,

“Do you understand what you’ve done? ‘Fate’ is······.”

“I know! That’s why I’m asking you for help, Yoo Joonghyuk-ssi.”

Yoo Joonghyuk’s mind became a tangle.

The Moerae’s ‘fate’ was not merely a power to see and foretell the future.

Rather, the prophecy was closer to a ‘conclusion’ drawn through ‘big data’.

The ‘most reasonable future’, predicted through a combination of countless stories.

Viewed this way, ‘fate’ might seem far from absolute, something that could be changed any number of ways. But that was by no means the case.

Because <Olympus>’s prophecies had never once been wrong.

Even Zeus, the chief god of <Olympus>, had been unable to escape that ‘fate’.

Because the moment a fate began, the probability of all of <Olympus> was used to make it come true.

“Please stop Kim Dokja-ssi. Otherwise······.”

Yoo Sangah’s desperate words could go no further.

Bzzzzzt.

The forbidden probability caused Yoo Sangah to collapse unconscious amid the sparks. But Yoo Joonghyuk could clearly read the text of the skein embroidered in the air behind her.

「Incarnation Kim Dokja will die at the hands of the person he loves most.」

●

“Whoa, these plains are huge!”

“Is this really the ‘Dark Castle’?”

Lee Hyunsung stared in apparent wonder at the endless horizon.

Vast plains, with stretches of jungle spread here and there.

An ominous, pitch-black river flowed majestically through the middle, dividing the plains in two.

That river was probably [Phoenix], a tributary from the Demon Realm.

At last, we had reached the Dark Castle’s second floor.

“Yes. This is the second floor. It’s completely different from the first.”

Unlike the first floor, where a new scenario was underway, the Dark Castle’s second floor held a scenario that had been running for a very long time.

In the distance, I could see incarnations gathered in groups, talking among themselves.

They seemed to be Seoul’s incarnations, who had newly entered along with us.

They showed no particular reaction when they saw us. Looking more closely, I saw that a dokkaebi was giving them guidance.

[······And so, congratulations to all you incarnations who have newly reached the second floor. These <Abyss Plains> will be a place of opportunity, where you can do anything.]

It was a dokkaebi I had never seen before.

The dokkaebi looked noticeably old, and seemed to have worked for the Bureau for a very long time.

Well, that made sense for someone in charge of the <Abyss Plains> scenario.

The scenario here was assigned to dokkaebis who had been demoted.

I turned on my smartphone and found the information about the Dark Castle’s second floor in ‘Ways of Survival’.

「The <Abyss Plains>. The dokkaebis call this place ‘the grave of scenarios’.」

······The grave of scenarios.

Seeing that expression stirred fresh feelings in me.

I’d already come this far.

Listening to the dokkaebi, Han Sooyoung spoke.

“More bullshit. Opportunity, my ass. They’ll fucking work us to death whenever they get the chance, spouting crap about adjusting the difficulty.”

She wasn’t the only one. The other incarnations, now accustomed to the dokkaebis’ sweet talk, simply glared at the dokkaebi with distrust.

Now that they’d already reached the ninth scenario, there was no way talk of opportunities or whatever else would work on them.

Whether the old dokkaebi had heard her or not, I didn’t know, but the dokkaebi smiled.

[Do not worry. The dokkaebis will not interfere in this scenario. Whether the scenario is entertaining or dull, we promise never to meddle with the story.]

The incarnations murmured.

No dokkaebi had ever said anything like that before.

Why were the dokkaebis, who always wanted more sensational stories, saying they would not interfere with the ‘story’ here?

“What the hell are you up to?”

“What’s that supposed to mean!”

[I know you are all weary from the scenarios thus far. But I speak the truth.]

[The updated main scenario has arrived!]

●

<Main Scenario # 9 ― ???>

Category: Main

Difficulty: ???

Clear Condition: ???

Time Limit: ―

Reward: None

Failure: ―

●

A scenario with all its conditions concealed, and neither a time limit nor a failure condition.

The incarnations, who had never received a scenario like this, were deeply bewildered.

“What? What are we supposed to do if you don’t reveal anything?”

“Fuck, you’re trying to screw us over with another shitty scenario, aren’t you?”

Even at the incarnations’ angry reactions, the dokkaebi simply smiled indulgently.

[What have you been striving for all this time? For family or friends? To become stronger? Or to reign over others? Each of you will have an answer. But I believe those answers are all lies. Because you have only come this far ‘to carry out the scenarios’.]

The incarnations’ gazes wavered at those words, which dismissed the lives they had been living lately.

The old dokkaebi continued.

[But it will be difficult to overcome the coming scenarios with that mindset alone. Such passive beings cannot survive in the <Star Stream>. Therefore, this scenario will demand nothing of you.]

A scenario that demanded nothing.

The incarnations shuddered.

[There is neither a time limit nor a failure condition. Because there is nothing to fail at. Find your own clear condition. Only those who find it will be able to move forward. Heh heh, though I wonder how many will make that choice... I do hope you will not fall asleep in this ‘grave’.]

With those final words, the dokkaebi vanished.

Suddenly deprived of a purpose, the incarnations filled the air with restless murmurs.

It was a strange sight.

Even though this scenario was more ‘peaceful’ than any they had experienced before, the incarnations seemed somehow anxious.

Like people who had been happier when they had an impossible goal.

Lee Hyunsung asked,

“Dokja-ssi? What on earth is this······?”

Lee Hyunsung also seemed deeply bewildered.

Until moments ago, he had been burning with determination to raise his ranking. Now a scenario ‘without a clear condition’ had suddenly appeared. He could only feel deflated. I had already been a little worried.

Because this might be the most dangerous scenario of all for our group.

Just as I was about to speak, I sensed someone stirring behind me.

“Ugh······ Where are we?”

Lee Jihye and Lee Gilyoung were regaining consciousness.

●

After checking her staggering rank of ‘98761st’, Lee Jihye sank into deep despair.

“I’ve never ranked this low, even on a mock exam······.”

Of course, that was a lie.

According to ‘Ways of Survival’, Lee Jihye wasn’t good at studying.

“······Dokja-hyung?”

Lee Gilyoung leaped like a grasshopper the moment he saw me. A little later, he curled up like a demure pill bug and pretended to be calm.

“I knew you’d be alive. I believed in you right to the end, hyung!”

Lee Jihye scoffed at that.

“What’s this little brat saying? You were crying with snot running down your face.”

“I wasn’t crying!”

Lee Gilyoung kept protesting that he hadn’t cried, insisting that of course he’d known I would come back to life.

But ten minutes later, his eyes brimming, Lee Gilyoung lost control of his emotions again and lunged at my thigh, shouting, “Hyuuuuung!”

“······A scenario without a scenario?”

A little later, after hearing our explanation, Lee Jihye looked at us as though asking what sort of bullshit that was.

“How do you clear something like that?”

After some thought, Lee Hyunsung said,

“Maybe there’s some hidden intention? If we find the hidden condition, I’m sure we’ll be able to clear the scenario.”

“Right? If we all work together and look······.”

Watching Lee Hyunsung and Lee Jihye join forces, I smiled wryly.

Sure enough, simplicity helped at times like this.

But not everyone possessed their straightforward drive.

“Um······ Do we really have to clear it?”

The speaker was Kim Yongpal of the Pink Kids.

Lee Jihye asked,

“Who’s that woman?”

“Just a woman······ a lady who happened to come along with us.”

I couldn’t be bothered to explain, so I glossed over it.

She wouldn’t believe me if I suddenly said he was a man in his forties.

Meanwhile, Kim Yongpal was still stammering, his eyes half glazed over.

“Wouldn’t it be all right to just stay as we are? Do we really have to clear it······?”

“What’s this bullshit all of a sudden?”

“······D-do any of you know what lies at the ‘end’ of these scenarios?”

It felt as though someone had pierced straight to the heart of the matter from an unexpected direction.

To think that man would have such a thought.

Taken aback, Lee Jihye asked,

“What?”

“W-we don’t know whether continuing to carry out the scenarios is good or bad for us······. In this endless succession of scenarios, we’re nothing but the constellations’ toys. Even if we clear this scenario, we don’t know what the next one will be like. We could die at a-any moment.”

Kim Yongpal’s words left my companions looking troubled.

Because, on reflection, he was right.

No one knew how these scenarios would end.

No one knew who would die, or where, or how.

Everyone had only come this far because ‘they would die if they didn’t clear them’.

But this scenario had neither a failure condition nor a time limit.

Biting her lip hard, Lee Jihye shouted,

“So what are you suggesting? That we stay here? Do you even know where we are? There are demon bastards roaming around. This place isn’t remotely safe······!”

But before Lee Jihye could finish, large demons began swarming toward us from across the plains. At a glance, they were grade 5 or stronger. Lee Jihye smiled as if to say she’d known it.

“See? They’re already coming.”

“Everyone, gather here!”

The nearby incarnations quickly gathered around our group. The approaching creatures were [Devil Bears], grade-4 demons. There were roughly twenty. If I used [Electrification] and joined forces with my companions, we could handle that number easily enough.

Of course, the other incarnations, who didn’t know my strength, looked despairing.

“Fuck······ More monsters like that······.”

That was when beams of light poured in from beyond the [Devil Bears].

Boom boom boom boom boom!

Pure white flames. A path of holy fire opened, and the [Devil Bears] at the rear let out piercing screams.

Power enough to slaughter even grade-4 demons.

That stigma was undoubtedly······.

“Unnie!”

Lee Jihye shouted.

Sure enough, those flames were Jung Heewon’s [Hell Flames Ignition].

Spotting us from afar, Jung Heewon looked startled.

In particular, the sight of me alive seemed to leave her almost aghast.

When I waved awkwardly, Jung Heewon hesitated, then nodded.

At that moment, a strange sense of something being off brushed past me.

······What was it?

Looking closely, I saw that Jung Heewon was riding a [Black Unicorn].

How had she tamed that beast?

Several others riding [Black Unicorns] alongside Jung Heewon drove back the [Devil Bears] and rapidly approached us. The incarnations who recognized Jung Heewon began chanting her name.

“Woooow! It’s the ‘Judge of Evil’!”

As Jung Heewon came close, Lee Jihye ran over.

“Unnie, I knew you’d be alive! Were you already here?”

“Jihye, I’m sorry, but let’s talk a little later.”

Leaving the chattering Lee Jihye behind, Jung Heewon immediately turned away. Looking crestfallen, Lee Jihye trudged back to my side. Jung Heewon was guiding the people with practiced ease, as though she was already accustomed to this.

“Everyone, follow me! I’ll take you somewhere safe!”

······Somewhere safe?

The unease I had felt earlier grew stronger.

Awed by Jung Heewon’s overwhelming strength, the incarnations followed her as though entranced. We had little choice but to follow, too. Had we crossed the plains for about an hour? A rampart hidden between stretches of jungle came into view.

A rampart so sturdy it seemed no demon could cross it.

As the incarnations stared in a daze, a voice sounded from somewhere.

[Welcome. It must have been difficult to come this far. You have endured so much. You are safe now.]

The people murmured.

Jung Heewon was looking at me, her eyes reflecting mixed emotions.

At that moment, I understood how this had happened.

Damn it. So that was it.

This was ‘that bastard’s’ fortress.

A man appeared atop the rampart.

A power that made you certain he was this place’s master merely by his presence there.

A demon harboring the most peaceful despair in the world looked down at us and smiled.

[You no longer need to carry out the scenarios.]

We no longer needed to carry out the scenarios.

At those words, everyone gathered at the fortress grew tense and alert.

“What the hell does that mean?”

Some people listened to him.

But most did not.

「He’s obviously a con artist.」

「······At least say something that makes sense. What? We don’t need to carry out the scenarios?」

「It must be a scheme to keep something all to himself.」

Whatever else they were, these were incarnations who had survived as far as the ninth scenario.

Even setting aside Cheon Inho of Geumho Station and Gong Pildu of Chungmuro, Seoul had been full of con artists. The incarnations here were either such swindlers themselves or people who had defeated them to make it this far.

So there was no way they would easily fall for sweet talk like that.

As though he had read their thoughts, the man on the rampart spoke.

[You will not believe me. I understand. Nine scenarios may hardly be called a long time, but neither can they be called a short one. I can well imagine what you have experienced, and what lives you have led to reach this place.]

A con artist’s basic technique was to pretend to understand the other person.

But these people were already sick of that ‘pretense’.

“You think we’ll fall for that again?”

“What the hell is your goal? What are you trying to say?”

Those who couldn’t hold back shouted first.

Then the man smiled faintly.

It was a smile so beautiful that you could hardly imagine him being a con artist.

[I mean exactly what I said. You no longer need to fight. I imagine the dokkaebis have explained it to you. The scenario here in the [Dark Castle] has neither a time limit nor a failure condition. Those of you who are clever will already have understood what that means.]

When I looked beside me, Kim Yongpal of the Pink Kids had a gleam in his eyes.
